analysis:
Examined all three primary analyses and the available replayed source. SandboxInstaller.swift's patch adds disk paths to setup options and forwards repeated --disk/value argument pairs to both planning and installation (head 128–137). Capability detection is a substring check (head 107–110), not authentication. Paths are separate arguments, so this change does not itself establish shell injection. BASE lines 41–95 and 134–154 show existing HTTPS download restrictions, size limits and private staging; the supplied patch does not weaken them. SandboxTestSupport.swift head 187–201 adds fake capability and plan-stderr behavior, not production controls.
The changes concern TB-013/T-061 and A-019: installer execution as the owner now carries external-work-disk selections. A-018/T-059 are relevant to coordination with running jobs and provider availability. No supplied patch changes authorization, attestation, request encryption or billing. T-041 already covers external encrypted inference-cache storage; its protections cannot be assumed to apply to sandbox VM/job storage, and no cache modification is established here.
No independently supported regression qualifies for a finding. Material questions remain unresolved because replay omits nine reviewed units and does not supply SandboxWorkDisk or the add-on installer implementation. Further review must verify SandboxSetupCommand.swift head 156–186, 291–367, 419–446 and 480–485 against the reported validation/refusal behavior; inspect absolutePath/check/enableOwnership for privileged command selection and path handling; and validate the installer's disk parsing, permissions, mount replacement/disconnection and running-job contract. The changed CLI documentation and status/work-disk tests are also incompletely replayed. Determine whether TB-013/A-019 need expanded coverage for ownership enablement and external VM storage. These are coverage limits and unverified contracts, not observed missing controls.
